messages:
alex: Quick eyes needed on a TF change — PR ready: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/5423. Adds gpu node labels + ENI safety constraints to the gpu-pool module. No planned replacements per `terraform plan`, but would like another pair of eyes before I merge. target: merge before tomorrow's canary window.
sam: on it. quick q — are we changing eni_count or lifecycle?
alex: changing `max_enis = 1` for the pool and adding `prevent_destroy = true` on the eni attachment resource. also added `create_before_destroy = false` so we don't churn nodes. plan shows only updates, not recreates. snippet in PR description.
lina: will review after lunch. can you add an explicit migration note in the PR body for terraform state expectations? last time that saved us.
alex: good call — added a short migration section and the `plan` output. also included rollback steps (revert module version + apply).
infra-ci-bot: terraform plan: SUCCESS — no replacements detected in predicted plan (0 to add, 3 to change, 0 to destroy). full output: https://ci.redwood/plan/98765
dan: FYI i can approve around 14:00 PST. prefer merge in 14:30-15:00 window and start canary at 15:00 for 30m (10% traffic).
sam: quick review done — left one minor nit about a module var name (rename `gpu_label` -> `node_gpu_label`) and a comment about SG rules. otherwise LGTM.
alex: thanks — pushed the var rename and tightened the SG rule to only allow the management CIDR.
lina: approving from my side once sam's nit fixed. please add the manual rollback steps to the deployment runbook (link?).
alex: added runbook link and explicit `tfstate` rollback command. plan still clean. merging after dan approves. :thumbsup:
dan: approved. merge when ready — I'll watch canary and be on-call for the window.
alex: merged and kicked off the apply. will post status once canary looks good.
infra-ci-bot: apply started: https://ci.redwood/apply/12345 — ETA ~6m
sam: nice, watching logs.
alex: canary healthy at +15m, latency and error rate within baseline. final percent rollout in 10m.
dan: all good from my side. great job.
alex: closing the thread — thanks everyone! :rocket:
